faq.question: How do I create a MediTap account?
faq.answer: From the log in page, choose Create an account. Enter a username, email, and password. After registration you can sign in and complete your patient intake.

faq.question: I forgot my password. What should I do?
faq.answer: On the log in page, choose Forgot password and enter your account email. We will send a secure link to reset your password. The link expires after use; request a new one if needed.

faq.question: My PDF upload did not parse correctly. What can I do?
faq.answer: Try a clearer scan or export from your health portal. After upload, review extracted fields in Patient Information and correct anything that looks wrong. Staff can also verify before relying on parsed data.

faq.question: How does staff editing work?
faq.answer: Patients can upload documents and review their information. Authorized staff unlock editing from the intake or admin screens using staff credentials—without signing the patient out.

faq.question: Is Epic integration required?
faq.answer: No. Epic FHIR sandbox linking is optional and is configured from the Admin panel after you log in, for pilots and technical demonstrations.

faq.question: Who can I contact for privacy or HIPAA questions?
faq.answer: Use the Privacy or account security category above, or email support@meditap.ai. For clinical emergencies, contact your provider or emergency services directly—MediTap support cannot provide medical advice.

about.title: About MediTap
about.subtitle: Closing the gap between fragmented health records and the intake workflows care teams rely on.
about.problemBody: Despite decades of investment in digital health, clinicians still lack a unified, bedside-ready view of the patient story. MyChart, HIEs, and lab networks each hold part of the puzzle—but none deliver complete context at the moment of care.
about.solutionBody: MediTap empowers patients to carry their medical history across networks with consent-first sharing and fast intake—from structured forms and uploaded PDFs and images.
solutionItems: Staff workflows for review and chart updates
Epic FHIR sandbox-ready for health-system pilots
about.whoBody: Hospitals, clinics, and digital health partners evaluating faster onboarding, better data quality at intake, and interoperable connections to existing EHR investments.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.subtitle: These terms govern your use of the MediTap patient intake and health-record workflow platform, including your authorization for clinical use of the information you provide.

s1.title: 1. Acceptance
s1.p1: By creating an account, logging in, uploading documents, or otherwise using MediTap, you agree to these Terms of Service and to our <privacyLink>Privacy Policy</privacyLink>. If you do not agree, do not use the service.
s1.p2: Where you act on behalf of another person (for example, as a parent, legal guardian, or authorized representative), you represent that you have lawful authority to accept these terms and to provide that person's health information through MediTap.

s2.title: 2. The service
s2.p1: MediTap helps patients and authorized care teams capture, review, and manage health intake information, including document upload and optional integrations such as Epic FHIR sandbox connectivity for demonstration and development purposes.
s2.p2: MediTap is a technology platform that supports clinical workflows. It does not replace in-person evaluation, emergency services, or the professional judgment of licensed healthcare providers.

s3.title: 3. Accounts and access
s3.p1: You are responsible for safeguarding your login credentials and for activity under your account.
items: Notify your organization or MediTap support if you suspect unauthorized access.
Staff and administrative features require appropriate roles assigned by your organization.

s4.title: 4. Authorization for Medical and Clinical Use of Your Information
s4.lead: By creating an account, accessing, or using MediTap, you voluntarily authorize MediTap, your participating healthcare organization, and authorized members of your care team to collect, receive, store, review, process, use, and disclose the health-related information you enter, upload, import, or otherwise provide through the platform for legitimate healthcare, treatment, payment, and healthcare operations purposes, as permitted by applicable law.
s4.hipaaP1: MediTap is designed to support compliance with the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA), the Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health (HITECH) Act, and other applicable federal and state privacy laws. When MediTap processes Protected Health Information ("PHI") on behalf of a covered healthcare provider or other HIPAA-regulated entity, the collection, storage, use, and disclosure of PHI are performed in accordance with applicable legal requirements, contractual obligations, and this Authorization.
s4.hipaaP2: Please note that HIPAA applies only where MediTap is acting on behalf of a HIPAA-covered entity or Business Associate. Certain features or uses of the platform may not be subject to HIPAA but remain governed by this Privacy Policy and applicable law.
s4.authIntro: By using MediTap, you authorize us to:
authItems: Build, maintain, update, and securely store your patient intake record, longitudinal health summary, and related clinical documentation.

Collect and organize demographic information, emergency contacts, insurance information, allergies, medications, immunizations, laboratory results, diagnoses, procedures, visit history, vital signs, and other health information that you choose to provide or authorize us to retrieve.

Support medical treatment, care coordination, referrals, patient intake, billing support, quality improvement, operational workflows, and other healthcare-related services performed by authorized healthcare professionals.
Display your information through dashboards, patient summaries, intake workflows, and other clinical tools that assist healthcare professionals in delivering care.

Process documents that you upload, including PDFs, scanned medical records, insurance documents, and laboratory reports, using automated document recognition and data extraction technologies to identify structured information and pre-populate intake fields.

Synchronize or display information from authorized third-party integrations that you or your healthcare organization enable, including electronic health record systems such as Epic FHIR integrations or other supported healthcare data connections.
Improve platform functionality, security, reliability, and user experience using de-identified or aggregated information whenever possible and as permitted by applicable law.
s4.authNote: Automated document processing is intended solely to assist administrative and clinical workflows. Healthcare professionals remain responsible for reviewing and verifying medical information before relying upon it for diagnosis, treatment, or other clinical decisions.
s4.repIntro: By submitting information through MediTap, you represent and warrant that:
repItems: The information you provide is submitted voluntarily.
To the best of your knowledge, the information is accurate, complete, and not intentionally misleading.
You are either the patient identified in the record, or legally authorized to provide information and grant this authorization on behalf of the patient.

You agree to update information when material changes occur, including medication changes, allergies, emergency contacts, insurance information, or other significant health information, if you continue using MediTap.
s4.accessIntro: Access to your information is limited to individuals and systems with a legitimate need to know and is governed by role-based access controls and organizational policies.
accessItems: You, through your authenticated MediTap account.
Authorized physicians, nurses, medical assistants, administrative personnel, and other members of your healthcare team acting within the scope of their assigned responsibilities.
Authorized personnel temporarily granted elevated access in accordance with your healthcare organization's policies, including shared-device workflows where permitted.
Service providers that securely host, maintain, operate, or support MediTap under contractual confidentiality, privacy, and security obligations.

Third-party healthcare organizations, health information exchanges, laboratories, pharmacies, or integration partners only when you or your healthcare organization explicitly authorize or enable those connections.
s4.accessMinimumNecessary: MediTap follows the HIPAA "Minimum Necessary" standard whenever applicable, limiting access to the minimum amount of Protected Health Information reasonably necessary for authorized users to perform their assigned responsibilities, except where broader access is required for treatment or otherwise permitted by law.
s4.securityIntro: Protecting your health information is one of MediTap's highest priorities.
s4.securityIntro2: MediTap implements administrative, technical, and physical safeguards designed to protect Protected Health Information and other personal information from unauthorized access, alteration, disclosure, or destruction. These safeguards may include:
securityItems: Encryption of data during transmission using industry-standard protocols.
Encryption of stored data where applicable.
Routine security updates and vulnerability management.
Continuous monitoring and security improvements designed to protect patient information.
s4.securityClosing: While no electronic system can guarantee absolute security, MediTap continuously works to implement reasonable and appropriate safeguards consistent with applicable healthcare privacy and security standards.
s4.emergencyBody: Where permitted by applicable law and authorized by your participating healthcare organization, MediTap may allow authorized healthcare professionals to access limited health information during emergency situations when necessary to protect your health or safety or the health or safety of another individual. Emergency access is logged and monitored in accordance with organizational policies and applicable legal requirements.
s4.privacyRightsIntro: Subject to applicable federal and state law, you may have the right to:
privacyRightsItems: Request access to your health information.
Request corrections or amendments to inaccurate information.
Request restrictions on certain uses or disclosures of your information.
Request confidential communications through alternative methods where applicable.
Receive an accounting of certain disclosures of your Protected Health Information.
Receive copies of applicable privacy notices.
Withdraw or limit authorizations where permitted by law.
s4.privacyRightsClosing: Requests may be submitted through your participating healthcare organization or by contacting MediTap Support.
s4.willNotIntro: Unless required or permitted by law, MediTap will not:
willNotItems: Share your medical information with unauthorized third parties.
Use your Protected Health Information for advertising or marketing purposes without your authorization where required by law.
Allow employees, contractors, or service providers to access your information except as necessary to perform authorized job responsibilities.
Disclose your information except as authorized by you, required by law, permitted under applicable healthcare privacy laws, or necessary to provide healthcare services.
s4.retentionBody: This authorization remains effective while you maintain an active MediTap account or while your healthcare organization retains records in accordance with applicable medical record retention laws, organizational policies, or other legal obligations. You may request to withdraw or limit your authorization by contacting your participating healthcare organization or MediTap Support. Withdrawal of authorization may limit or disable certain MediTap features and does not require deletion of information already incorporated into an official medical record or retained as required by applicable law.
s4.breachBody: If MediTap becomes aware of a breach involving unsecured Protected Health Information, we will investigate the incident promptly and respond in accordance with applicable federal and state laws, including HIPAA Breach Notification requirements where applicable. Where required by law, affected individuals, participating healthcare organizations, and appropriate regulatory authorities will be notified within the legally required timeframes.
s4.contactIntro: If you have questions regarding this Authorization, your privacy rights, or MediTap's handling of your information, please contact:
s4.closing: By continuing to use MediTap, you acknowledge that you have read, understood, and agree to this Authorization for Medical and Clinical Use of Your Information.

s5.title: 5. Health information and regulatory responsibility
s5.p1: MediTap is designed to support clinical workflows. Your healthcare organization remains responsible for compliance with applicable laws (including HIPAA and state privacy laws where applicable), obtaining any additional consents required for your jurisdiction, and determining how information is used in production care environments.
s5.p2: MediTap does not provide medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. Clinical decisions remain the responsibility of licensed providers who review your record and evaluate you directly.

s6.title: 6. Document upload and imported records
s6.p1: When you upload documents or authorize import from external systems, you confirm that you have the right to share those materials for clinical intake purposes and that they relate to your care (or the care of the individual you represent).
s6.p2: Automated parsing may suggest field values that require human verification. You agree that parsed or synced data should be reviewed by you and/or authorized staff before being relied upon for clinical decisions.

s7.title: 7. Acceptable use
s7.p1: You may not misuse MediTap, attempt to breach security, reverse engineer the service except as permitted by law, upload unlawful or harmful content, or enter information about another person without proper authorization.

s8.title: 8. Emergency and urgent care
s8.p1: MediTap is not for medical emergencies. If you think you may have a medical emergency, call your local emergency number (for example, 911 in the United States) or go to the nearest emergency department immediately. Do not rely on MediTap for time-sensitive or life-threatening situations.

s9.title: 9. Changes and contact
s9.p1: We may update these terms from time to time. Material changes will be reflected on this page with an updated date. Continued use after changes constitutes acceptance of the revised terms.
s9.p2: Questions about these terms or your authorization: contact us through the <supportLink>Support</supportLink> page or your participating healthcare organization.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.subtitle: How MediTap handles information when you use our platform.
privacy.overviewBody: MediTap respects your privacy. This policy describes the types of information we process when you use the application and the choices available to you.
collectItems: Account information such as username, email, and authentication credentials.
Patient intake data you enter or upload (for example demographics, medications, allergies).
Technical logs needed to operate and secure the service (device/browser, timestamps, errors).
useItems: Provide login, intake, dashboard, and staff workflow features.
Improve reliability, security, and product quality.
Support optional integrations you or your organization enable (such as Epic FHIR sandbox linking).
privacy.sharingBody: We do not sell personal health information. Data may be shared with your healthcare organization, service providers that help us host and operate MediTap, or when required by law.
privacy.securityBody: We apply administrative, technical, and organizational safeguards appropriate to a health technology platform. Retention periods depend on your organization's policies and applicable regulations.
privacy.choicesBody: You may request access, correction, or deletion of your account data through your care organization or via our <supportLink>Support</supportLink> contact form.
